extracted.intended_audience: policy makers, IP office statisticians, patent researchers and practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, metrics and reporting caveats used in WIPO's patent statistics (applications, grants, patents in force, examination outcomes, utility models, pendency and residency classifications). Useful for compiling, comparing or interpreting patent data across offices and jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent offices must assess whether the claims made in applications meet the standards of novelty, non-obviousness and industrial applicability defined in national laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These substantive legal standards (novelty, inventive step/non-obviousness, industrial applicability) are applied by offices during examination and consume time and resources. They are defined in national laws and may differ in application across jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term (duration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent rights generally last for up to 20 years from the date an application is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the statutory term is typically up to 20 years, actual effective duration depends on maintenance payments and whether the holder lets the patent lapse earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance/renewal fee requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A holder must pay a maintenance/renewal fee in order for a patent to remain valid, and may opt to let a patent lapse before the end of its full term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting examples: for 92 offices with in‑force data by filing year, ~40.3% of patents granted remained in force for at least 8 years after filing and ~18.1% lasted the full 20‑year term. Maintenance behaviour affects counts of patents in force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications pending (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications pending is defined as all patent applications, at any stage in the process, awaiting a final decision by a patent office, including those applications for which applicants have not filed a request for examination (where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes applications awaiting a request for examination. Offices with a high share of pending applications awaiting a request for examination have limited scope to reduce their stock of pending applications because examination cannot start until the request is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination outcome categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent examination outcomes are categorised as granted, rejected or withdrawn/abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistics present shares and absolute numbers by outcome (e.g., rejected shares by office, withdrawn/abandoned shares). Note: data are compiled from offices that reported these categories (around 80 offices in 2021).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not compare application-year data with grant-year data
rubrics_metrics.description: Application data for a given year should not be compared with grant data from the same year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a time lag between filing and grant (procedural delays); grants in a given year usually derive from applications filed in earlier years, so direct year‑to‑year comparisons are misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-country comparison caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination processes differ across offices, which makes cross-country comparisons difficult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WIPO makes every effort to compile outcomes based on common definitions and concepts, but differences in procedures, examination capacity and delays mean comparisons must be interpreted with caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident vs non-resident classification and shares
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistics distinguish resident and non-resident applications/grants (resident = applicants domiciled in the office's jurisdiction; non-resident = applicants from abroad).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures include resident and non-resident shares for applications and grants by office. The resident/non-resident mix affects interpretations (e.g., some offices' growth driven by non-resident filings). See definitions/glossary for precise residency rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin determination and equivalent application counting
rubrics_metrics.description: The origin of a patent application is determined by the residence of the first named applicant. Applications filed at regional offices are considered equivalent to multiple applications in the relevant member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WIPO reports both absolute origin counts and 'equivalent application' counts (the latter treats regional filings as multiple national equivalents). Choice of counting method affects origin totals and comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model (UM) definition and distinct treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility model (UM) is a special form of patent right granted by a state or jurisdiction to an inventor or the inventor’s assignee for a fixed time period; terms and conditions differ slightly from those for normal patents, including a shorter term of protection and less stringent eligibility requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UM filings and grants are reported separately. Jurisdictional practices vary widely (e.g., China accounts for the vast majority of UM filings worldwide). Policy or legislative changes (such as Australia's phase‑out of its innovation patent) affect UM filing patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendency metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Average pendency times (e.g., for first office action and for final decision) are tracked as key procedural metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pendency figures are presented by office and are influenced by factors such as examination capacity, backlog, and whether applicants must request examination. High pendency affects the time between application filing and grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data coverage and comparability notes (WIPO estimates and methodological breaks)
rubrics_metrics.description: World totals in WIPO tables are estimates using data covering a defined number of patent offices; some national time series may not be comparable due to methodological changes (e.g., China pre‑2017 data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should note methodological breaks and the set of reporting offices when interpreting trends or computing growth rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant-rate interpretation warning
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents granted out of total processed applications data presented here should not be interpreted as the 'grant rate.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presented ratio may not reflect simple grant propensity because of differences in processing definitions, timing, which applications are included in 'processed', and cross‑office heterogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of resident/non-resident contribution decomposition for growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Growth (or decline) at an office is decomposed into contributions from resident and non-resident applications/grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures show total growth broken down by contributions of resident vs non‑resident filings/grants (useful to identify whether growth is driven by domestic activity or by foreign applicants).
